context: PT track 3 branch shadow-tech-lead off v0.11.1: probe harness (sandboxed executor wired as probe_fn), shadow Tech Lead (full structured adjudication, non-binding, gate-invariant), P0 shadow reason_check + trace-gate logging, P1 basis-evidence-gated precedent reasons, P2 raise-time function keys + qualified-name precedent lookup with miss telemetry + TL eligibility boundary assertion, acceptance runner for the 48-case known-answer corpus. Suite 458 green.

reviewer_reports.summary: The probe harness wiring introduces a reachable API mismatch that will break shadow adjudication probes at runtime, and the new test probe mode no longer runs tests under the project test runner, which can make valid test probes fail spuriously.

findings.title: Shadow adjudication calls probe_fn with the wrong signature
findings.recommendation: Call the probe function with the same contract documented and implemented elsewhere, passing both the finding and the request, e.g. probe_fn(finding, json.dumps(spec)) or probe_fn(finding, spec). Add an integration test that exercises a needs_probe shadow adjudication through make_probe_fn to catch this mismatch.

findings.title: Test probes are executed as plain Python scripts instead of via the test runner
findings.recommendation: Run kind 'test' probes through the project's supported test runner rather than invoking the target file directly. At minimum, use a command that preserves normal test discovery and fixtures, and add coverage for a test target that only passes when executed by the runner.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff only adds tests and does not itself introduce a demonstrated correctness or security defect. I did not find a supported, reachable issue grounded in the added lines alone.
The new acceptance runner and CLI wiring introduce a reachable crash on empty corpora and a silent contract break where the documented timeout parameter is ignored during paraphrase mutations.

findings.recommendation: Guard the overall-accuracy calculation the same way M2 and M5 are guarded, for example by returning 0.0 or a sentinel when 'len(scores) == 0', and make the gate logic handle that case explicitly.

findings.title: Paraphrase mutation ignores the timeout argument promised by the API
findings.recommendation: Pass the provided timeout through to the seat call if the seat API supports it, or remove the unused parameter and update the docstring so callers are not misled into thinking paraphrase calls are bounded by this function.

reviewer_reports.summary: All three test files are well-formed and pass under the supported POSIX+Python 3.11+ configuration; no production-risk issues detected.

The acceptance runner lacks a timeout guard on paraphrase LLM calls, risking unbounded execution and resource exhaustion; also, the M4 mutation flip-rate denominator can be zero when mutations are disabled, causing a division-by-zero error that crashes the metric calculation.

findings.recommendation: Review all callers of function_key to ensure the redefinition does not break existing behavior, or rename one of the definitions to avoid shadowing.
